visuals.at: Review quiz, so it's longer. Ten questions
visuals.title: Review quiz
visuals.text: Ten questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Which team owns the long-term client relationship?
questions.explain: Coverage teams own the relationship; product teams such as mergers and acquisitions bring the specialist execution.
questions.explain_at: Coverage teams are organised by industry and own the client relationship

questions.q: Tax at 25%. EBITDA is 200, depreciation 50, interest 30. What's net income?
questions.explain: EBIT 150, pre-tax income 120, tax 30, net income 90. Skipping tax gives 120, skipping interest 112.5, skipping depreciation 127.5.
questions.explain_at: Revenue, minus cost of goods sold, gives gross profit

questions.q: Why add depreciation back on the cash flow statement?

options.text: It cut profit, but no cash left
It's a financing item, not operating

questions.explain: Depreciation reduced net income, but the cash left when the asset was bought, not in this period.
questions.explain_at: add back ten of depreciation, cash up two point five

questions.q: A company issues 50 of new shares for cash. What changes on the balance sheet?
questions.explain: New shareholders hand over cash, so cash and equity both rise by 50.
questions.explain_at: Because every asset was paid for somehow

questions.q: A company repays 40 of debt with cash. What happens to net income?
questions.explain: Repaying debt isn't an expense. Only the interest hits the income statement.
questions.explain_at: Five: nothing. Repaying debt isn't an expense

questions.q: Tax at 25%. Depreciation goes up by 20. What happens to cash?
questions.explain: The extra depreciation cuts the tax bill by 20 × 25% = 5. The depreciation itself doesn't move cash.
questions.explain_at: Depreciation goes up by ten, tax rate twenty-five percent. Go.

questions.q: Receivables fall by 10. What happens to cash?
questions.explain: Customers paid what they owed, so cash came in: an asset going down releases cash.
questions.explain_at: Net income is eighty, depreciation twenty, receivables go up by fifteen

questions.q: What's the difference between book value and market value of equity?
questions.explain: Book value comes from the balance sheet; market value is share price times shares and reflects expected future earnings.
questions.explain_at: Eight: book value is the accounting value

questions.q: Which is a legitimate adjustment to EBITDA?

options.text: Marketing, since it varies each year
Stock-based pay, as it isn't cash
A genuine one-off, like a settlement

questions.explain: A one-off cost can come out if it really doesn't come back. Marketing and head office are the costs WeWork stripped out.
questions.explain_at: It stripped out costs like marketing and head office

questions.q: A buyer pays 800 million for a business with 200 million of revenue. What's the revenue multiple?
questions.explain: 800 ÷ 200 = 4x revenue, the same sum as Eaton's 810 over 250 for COL.
questions.explain_at: Eight hundred and ten over two hundred and fifty
